# Maiya: Super Nature Girl — changelog

The ROM sets shared with the NeoGeoSDK v1.7.1 pre-release. The SDK keeps its
own version; Maiya's ROMs are numbered on their own (`_v1`, `_v2`, ...).

## v2 (2026-10-03) — everything since v1

v1 was built on 2026-09-29. v2 is that game made smoother, cleaner and
safer to boot, on every system it targets.

### Smoother play

- **A steady frame rate.** Every stage now runs at about 59 frames a
  second. Measured before this work, the game overran its frame on 24–89%
  of frames (50–59 fps, with visible slowdowns). In v2 that is 0–4%, and in
  play nearly none. Measured over every stage's road and every guardian's
  arena: 23 scenarios of 3,600 frames each.
- **No half-drawn frames.** Sprites and HUD text are written to video
  memory during the vertical blank, all at once. The screen is never drawn
  from sprite tables halfway through an update, which removes tearing and
  one-frame glitches when many things move.
- **Sound never holds the game up.** Sound commands queue and go out while
  the game keeps running. In v1 each one waited for the sound driver's
  reply, up to 38,000 cycles when the reply was missed (as in MAME). All
  341 bytes of a test run were checked arriving at the Z80, none lost.
- **Characters keep their sprites between frames.** Only what changed
  (position, frame, palette, flip, size) reaches video memory, instead of
  the whole character every frame.
- **No sprite flicker between equal-height characters.** Two characters at
  the same height used to swap drawing order; now they keep it.
- **At most 78 sprites on a line,** measured on every stage, so no
  sprite drops out (the hardware draws 96).
- **HUD text** writes only the characters that changed.
- **Faster fades:** a fade's colour costs 78 cycles instead of 200.
- **Creature animations** use the 68000's own division instead of slow
  library calls (20 a frame on the Sunken Reef).
- No library multiply or divide is left in a frame's work.

### Clean scene changes

- **No glitches between screens.** Every scene change now happens behind a
  fade. The old screen fades to black (white for the chooser), the new one
  is built while nothing shows, and it fades up whole. This covers:
  - Start to the chooser;
  - the chooser to the reminders, and on to the first mission;
  - each mission start, and a retry;
  - a guardian's defeat to the flight over the healed valley;
  - the bonus round and the elder's briefing;
  - the ending.

  This removes, among others:
  - a torn half-white frame after Start;
  - the chooser's title left on a black frame;
  - a leftover sprite under the reminders;
  - a mission's painting and HUD appearing piece by piece;
  - a few frames of scrambled tiles before the flight over the healed
    valley.
- **A beaten guardian** lies grey, then goes in a puff of dust and sparks.
  It no longer darkens into a black shape on the road.
- **The chooser has a clock:** 15 seconds to choose (shown top right),
  then the girl picked answers the call.
- **The reminders move on by themselves.** "How to play" and the story
  each stay 10 seconds, or until a button.
- **See their moves.** On "how to play", A and B together brings out Maiya
  and Luna face to face over the forest. Both play each move, with its
  name and keys: run, jump, whip, thorn, dash, Rose Blossom Surge, Rising
  Bloom, the high leap and the Secret Art. Any button goes back.

### Living backgrounds

- **No more seam.** Each valley's far painting used to wrap every 512
  pixels with a hard line where its two ends met, cross-faded into a
  doubled image. It now wraps along a cut that follows where its ends look
  alike, so the join can't be seen and nothing is doubled.
- **Longer paintings, less repetition.**
  - Five valleys show their whole painted band, about 1,100-1,200 pixels
    of scenery, before it comes round again: the forest, the World Tree's
    marsh, the works, the Sky Road and the citadel.
  - The other seven are twice as long as before, their painting followed
    by its mirror image, which meets it edge to edge.
  - The far layer streams the painting a column at a time as she travels.
- **Ground to walk on.** The road is the painting's own ground, wrapping
  without a seam, wherever the far painting goes.
- **Small life, far off.** Each valley has a few creatures and lights of
  its own in the air between the HUD and the road. They are drawn small
  and drift with the far painting, so they read as part of the distance:
  - forest: butterflies and sun motes;
  - falls: butterflies and mist;
  - coast: glints and spray;
  - autumn grove: falling leaves;
  - grotto: snow and ice glints;
  - World Tree: fireflies and petals;
  - works and citadel: embers and smoke;
  - reef: bubbles and light;
  - cave: glints and fireflies;
  - savanna: pollen and butterflies;
  - Sky Road: snow.

### Guardians

- **The health bar tells the truth.** It closes a quarter of the gap each
  frame instead of a pixel at a time, and keeps moving after the last
  blow. Before, a big hit could leave it a second behind, and it froze
  where it was when the guardian fell, so guardians seemed to die with
  health left.
- **The fliers fall sooner:**
  - the Smog Dreadnought on the Sky Road takes 6 stomps' worth, down
    from 10;
  - the Blizzard Owl and the Iron Vulture take 5, down from 6.

### Her movement

- **A real run.** The sheet's four sprint poses all had the same leg in
  front and both fists up: she glided in one frozen stride. The run is now
  two strides — contact, legs passing under her, push-off, flight — with
  two more poses cut from her sheet. Her arms change with her legs, and she
  is the same size in every frame. She dips as a foot lands and while her
  legs pass, and rises in the flight between strides.
- **Starting and turning.** From a standstill she starts on a push-off.
  Turning at speed, she brakes low for a moment before running the other
  way, instead of running backwards.
- **The whole jump.** Push-off, rising, the top of the arc, falling —
  four poses where there were two.
- **No shadows.** The checkered shadows under Maiya, Luna, the creatures
  and the guardians are gone.

### New effects and feel

- **Heat haze** over the Golden Savanna: the horizon shimmers in 8-line
  bands, a raster effect on the display timer, at no cost to the frame
  rate.
- **Squash and stretch.** On landing Maiya squashes to 80% of her height
  and recovers over six frames. Springing up, she stretches tall and thin.
  Struck, both; striking, a little shorter. Her feet and her middle stay
  in place throughout.
- **Her run has weight:** on each footfall she dips a little (97% walking,
  95% running), so the run bobs twice a stride.
- **Living water and sky:** where a stage has a sky or waterfall pair of
  blues, they trade places every 16 frames, which reads as flowing water.
  It is off in guardian arenas.
- **Waterfall colours** stay in the falls' own palettes and no longer tint
  other scenery.
- **Cleaner small art:** flowers, mushrooms, coins and beetles were touched
  up at native resolution.

### Gameplay

- **The flying guardian is smaller,** with its hit regions scaled to match.
- **The flight's arena** begins earlier, so entering it no longer snaps
  Maiya backward.
- **Character select** updates only what changes on screen.

### Saves

- **Memory card saves on the AES.** Scores, names and progress go to the
  card, in a file called "MAIYA SCORES" (two card blocks).
  - The game reads the card at power-on and writes it when something is
    worth keeping: a game started, a name entered, the journey finished.
  - A blank card is formatted before the first save, never otherwise.
  - With no card, the game simply runs on.
  - Arcade boards keep their backup RAM as before.
- **Card saves under EagleBIOS too.** EagleBIOS now has a memory card
  routine that uses the same card layout as the console BIOS. One card
  carries its saves between EagleBIOS, the original AES BIOS and the
  Universe BIOS.
- **The MAME AES launchers insert a memory card** (tests\aes\memcard.bin),
  so console saves outlast MAME.

### Booting and sound on every system

- **MVS sound fix.** Sound on MVS boards, including after a multi-slot
  switch, and the coin and start sounds now work. In v1 they could go
  silent.
  - The sound driver keeps the system ROM's commands apart from the game's
    ($01 slot-switch wait, $02 eye-catcher, $03 reset, $09 game start).
  - A game byte that looks like a system command is sent escaped, so the
    two can never be confused.
  - A newly selected cartridge restarts its sound cleanly.
  - This first shipped as separate v1.7.1 test images; v2 has it in both
    builds.
- **Clean Universe BIOS splash.** The splash shows the Maiya logo on AES
  and on MVS. On MVS, v1 drew stray tiles there.
- **A simple AES boot:** one logo, no jingle, the same under EagleBIOS,
  the Universe BIOS and the original console BIOS. The game's own "Eagle
  Software presents" intro follows.
- **No garbled boot screens.** The system boot area and the game's font
  and HUD are kept apart:
  - The game's font and HUD sit in their own FIX banks.
  - The boot logo has its own sprite bank ($49).
  - The system ROM's tiles are left alone, so its screens and menus read
    correctly.
- **The Universe BIOS in-game menu** opens during play:
  - MVS: Start + Coin, or Start + A + B + C.
  - AES: Start + Select, or Start + A + B + C.

### Files and packaging

- **NeoSD images** are packed with the hardware alignment fixed after v1:
  P, S and M padded to 64 KiB, V padded to 8 MiB, C to 256 KiB. They have
  the same layout and size as v1 (P 512 KiB, S/M 128 KiB, V 8 MiB,
  C 8 MiB).
- **Darksoft folders** for both builds use the v1 layout. They are checked
  to turn back into the exact MAME ROMs.
- **MAME zips with EagleBIOS** for both builds, MVS and AES (v1 had
  only the AES one).
- **No original or third-party BIOS in any package.** v1's AES zips held
  the Universe BIOS or SNK's console BIOS. v2 carries only EagleBIOS, the
  open NeoGeoSDK system ROM; the .neo and Darksoft files carry no BIOS at
  all.
- Every v2 file is listed with its size, CRC32 and SHA-256 in
  `Maiya-MANIFEST_v2.txt`.

### Behind the scenes

- **The engine's public interface is frozen** (Framework 1.0), so later
  engine work can't break the game's calls.
- **One command, `make neo`,** builds the MAME sets and NeoSD images for
  both platforms.
- **Builds and tests run on EagleBIOS.**
- **Regression scenarios** (walking, climbing, guardians, continues, the
  tray, pits, flight) pass on it.
- **Checked in MAME** on MVS and AES, under EagleBIOS, the Universe BIOS
  4.0 and the original system ROMs: boot, title, play, sound and the
  in-game menu.

### Still open

- Real NeoSD, Darksoft, MVS and AES hardware: reports welcome.
- A run drawn frame by frame (eight poses of her own) would move better
  still than the cycle made from her sheet. Deeper parallax needs layered
  paintings, and the seven mirrored valleys would gain from paintings
  as long as the others'.

## v1 (2026-09-28/29)

The first preview:
- twelve valleys, two heroines, guardians, bonus rounds and the attract
  mode;
- MAME packages with EagleBIOS and with other BIOSes;
- NeoSD images for MVS and AES;
- Darksoft folders.

Later v1.7.1 test images (MVS sound fix, AES Universe BIOS fix, v3 tests)
were stepping stones to v2.
